Why not horizontal scroll

Scrolling a record table sideways takes the header — and therefore the sort affordance — off screen, and comparison across rows starts requiring you to hold an invisible column in your head. Those are the two things a table is for.

The one exception is a stat matrix, where every scrolling column shares a unit and comparing columns is the task. There, cards would destroy the grid that makes the numbers comparable, so it scrolls with the identifying column frozen.

Each table declares three things by hand: column priority, the one figure that survives to sm, and the secondary line. None of it can be derived.

Where 0px wins

Square cells with a 1px gap make the range render as one continuous bar. Material has to invent a pill with flat inner edges to get here; SeaKim gets it for free. This is the rare case where the radius rule produces a better object than the platform default rather than a constraint to work around.

Today is an underline

A fill means selected. A ring means focused. Both are taken — and a ring disappears once the date falls inside a range. A 2px bottom border is unambiguous and survives selection.

The grid is an affordance over a mono text input, never the only way in. There is no time picker: a time is a mono input, or a Select when the choices are real.

Slider

A fader, not a dial. Hover a track.

Price range$380–$460
Two thumbs may meet, never cross.
Max stops1
Ticks only when discrete and under 12 steps.

Why a bar and not a circle

A round thumb needs either a shadow or size to separate from a 4px track, and the system gives it neither. A bar taller than the track and narrower than it is tall reads as a mechanical fader position at 12px wide — and it never gets mistaken for a dot, a handle, or a checkbox.

The value is always text in the label row. No tooltip on the thumb: it would be an overlay following the finger, hidden under it on touch, and it would animate a number at exactly the moment the user is trying to read it.
